key_terms.لَغَائِظُونَ: They are constantly agitated or annoyed

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'They are always harassing us' mean in Surah Ash-Shu'ara?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Ash-Shu'ara (The Poets) describes the state of the disbelievers (specifically the Quraysh) who were constantly agitated, annoyed, and harassed by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers due to his message. It highlights the psychological and spiritual tension between the believers and the disbelievers during the Meccan period, reflecting the Shia understanding of 'ghaiz' as a deep-seated, enduring irritation that precedes divine retribution. The verse serves as a precursor to the promise of divine justice, assuring the faithful that their patience in the face of this persistent hostility is rewarded.
